TEMPERATURE_EXCURSION.label: Temperature Excursion / Reefer Failure
TEMPERATURE_EXCURSION.description: Cold chain breach — temperature deviation above recommended storage range during sea transit

commodity_wording.APPLE: The observed softening, internal browning, and accelerated decay of the Apple fruits is consistent with a temperature excursion above the recommended storage range of -1°C to +1°C during sea transit. The deviation from the prescribed set-point would have accelerated the rate of physiological activity, reducing firmness and shelf life of the consignment. This is further corroborated by the temperature recorder download findings.
commodity_wording.GRAPE: The observed shatter berry incidence, rachis browning, and surface mould development of the Table Grapes is consistent with SO₂ pad depletion and temperature excursions above the recommended storage range of -1°C to 0°C during sea transit. The elevated temperature conditions would have accelerated berry detachment, fungal proliferation, and deterioration of the bunch structure.
commodity_wording.KIWI: The observed premature softening, skin yellowing, and ethylene-driven over-ripening of the Kiwi fruits is consistent with a temperature excursion above the recommended storage range of -0.5°C to 0°C during sea transit. Exposure to elevated temperatures would have triggered accelerated ripening processes, reducing the commercial life of the consignment.
commodity_wording.MANDARIN: The observed peel softening, surface mould development, and rind breakdown of the Mandarin fruits is consistent with a temperature excursion above the recommended storage range of 2°C to 4°C during sea transit. The temperature deviation would have accelerated fungal proliferation and physiological breakdown of the peel tissue.
commodity_wording.ORANGE: The observed peel softening, rotten spot proliferation, and internal pulp breakdown of the Orange fruits is consistent with a temperature excursion above the recommended storage range of 4°C to 7°C during sea transit. Elevated temperatures would have accelerated fungal activity and internal quality deterioration.
commodity_wording.PEAR: The observed softening, flesh browning, and internal breakdown of the Pear fruits is consistent with a temperature excursion above the recommended storage range of -1°C to 0°C during sea transit. Exposure to elevated temperatures would have triggered chilling injury reversal and accelerated ripening, reducing the marketability of the consignment.
commodity_wording.BLUEBERRY: The observed skin collapse, juice leakage, surface mould, and fermentation of the Blueberry fruits is consistent with a temperature excursion above the recommended storage range of 0°C to +2°C during sea transit. The elevated temperature conditions would have accelerated the growth of Botrytis cinerea and other post-harvest pathogens, causing rapid commercial value loss.
commodity_wording.CHERRY: The observed pitting marks, skin softening, surface mould, and stem browning of the Cherry fruits is consistent with a temperature excursion above the recommended storage range of -1°C to +1°C during sea transit. Elevated temperatures would have accelerated post-harvest physiological changes and fungal activity in this highly perishable commodity.
commodity_wording.PLUM: The observed skin softening, juice leakage, and flesh browning of the Plum fruits is consistent with a temperature excursion above the recommended storage range of -1°C to +1°C during sea transit. The elevated temperature conditions would have accelerated internal breakdown and dramatically shortened the commercial life of the consignment.
commodity_wording.DRAGON: The observed scale browning, pulp softening, and surface mould development of the Dragon Fruits is consistent with a temperature excursion above the recommended storage range of 8°C to 12°C during sea transit. Dragon fruit is particularly susceptible to chilling injury at low temperatures and accelerated breakdown at elevated temperatures.
commodity_wording.AVOCADO: The observed accelerated ripening, skin blackening, and internal browning of the Avocado fruits is consistent with a temperature excursion above the recommended storage range of 5°C to 13°C (variety-dependent) during sea transit. Elevated ethylene production triggered by temperature fluctuation would have accelerated the ripening process beyond marketable condition.
commodity_wording._DEFAULT: The observed deterioration of the subject cargo is consistent with a temperature excursion above the recommended storage range during sea transit. The deviation from the prescribed reefer set-point would have accelerated the rate of physiological activity and decay, reducing the commercial value of the consignment.

PHYSIOLOGICAL_BREAKDOWN.label: Physiological Breakdown / Natural Senescence
PHYSIOLOGICAL_BREAKDOWN.description: Natural over-ripening or senescence — product was at or near end of shelf life at time of survey

commodity_wording.APPLE: The observed softening, flesh browning, and mealy texture of the Apple fruits is consistent with advanced physiological senescence and natural over-ripening. The product appears to have been at or near the end of its post-harvest shelf life at the time of the survey, possibly attributable to extended transit duration and/or pre-shipment storage in excess of recommended periods.
commodity_wording.GRAPE: The observed shatter berry incidence, rachis desiccation, and berry softening is consistent with natural senescence and progressive deterioration of the Table Grapes over an extended storage and transit period. Senescent changes are typical in this variety when held beyond the commercial shelf life window.
commodity_wording.KIWI: The observed over-ripening, flesh softening to press, and fermentation odour of the Kiwi fruits is consistent with natural senescence and advanced physiological breakdown, occurring when the product is held beyond its optimal commercial shelf life window.
commodity_wording.MANDARIN: The observed peel puffing, albedo breakdown, and segment desiccation of the Mandarin fruits is consistent with natural physiological ageing and senescence, typically arising when Mandarins are held beyond their recommended post-harvest storage period.
commodity_wording.ORANGE: The observed peel breakdown, internal segment drying, and reduced juice content of the Orange fruits is consistent with natural post-harvest senescence, typically observed when the product is held beyond its optimal commercial storage period.
commodity_wording.PEAR: The observed flesh mealiness, internal breakdown, and core browning of the Pear fruits is consistent with advanced physiological senescence. Pears are climacteric fruits subject to rapid deterioration once the ripening process is initiated, and the condition observed suggests the product had progressed beyond its optimal commercial stage.
commodity_wording.BLUEBERRY: The observed skin shrinkage, loss of bloom, and fermentation of the Blueberry fruits is consistent with natural post-harvest senescence. Blueberries have a limited shelf life window, and the observed condition suggests the product had progressed beyond its optimal commercial stage at time of survey.
commodity_wording.CHERRY: The observed colour deepening, softening, and stem desiccation of the Cherry fruits is consistent with natural post-harvest senescence. Cherries are extremely perishable and sensitive to handling, with the observed condition suggesting the product had progressed beyond its optimal commercial marketability window.
commodity_wording.PLUM: The observed flesh softening, translucency, and juice leakage of the Plum fruits is consistent with natural post-harvest senescence and over-ripening. Plums are climacteric fruits that undergo rapid deterioration once the ripening process advances beyond the commercial optimum.
commodity_wording.DRAGON: The observed scale browning, bract tip desiccation, and pulp softening of the Dragon Fruits is consistent with natural post-harvest senescence, typically observed when the product is held beyond its optimal commercial storage and transit period.
commodity_wording.AVOCADO: The observed skin blackening, flesh softening, and internal browning of the Avocado fruits is consistent with natural physiological ripening and senescence. Avocados are highly perishable climacteric fruits, and the observed condition suggests the product had progressed beyond the window of commercial acceptability.
commodity_wording._DEFAULT: The observed deterioration of the subject cargo is consistent with natural post-harvest senescence and physiological breakdown. The product appears to have been at or near the end of its commercial shelf life at the time of the survey.

TRANSIT_DELAY.label: Transit Delay — Extended Beyond Shelf Life
TRANSIT_DELAY.description: Consignment was in transit for longer than the commodity's recommended shelf life permits

commodity_wording.APPLE: The observed deterioration of the Apple fruits is consistent with an extended transit duration that exceeded the recommended shelf life window for this commodity. Apple fruits require a controlled atmosphere transit period of approximately 4–6 weeks; any transit duration in excess of this, particularly in the absence of controlled atmosphere, will result in accelerated ripening, firmness loss, and decay.
commodity_wording.GRAPE: The observed condition of the Table Grapes is consistent with a transit delay that extended the total cold chain exposure beyond the recommended window for this commodity. Table Grapes from South Africa typically require a total transit time of 21–28 days; extended periods result in progressive SO₂ pad depletion, rachis browning, and berry shatter.
commodity_wording.KIWI: The observed over-ripening and softening of the Kiwi fruits is consistent with an extended transit duration. Kiwi fruits require storage at approximately -0.5°C with controlled atmosphere to achieve a shelf life of up to 6 months; however, any delay in transit combined with ethylene exposure will substantially accelerate ripening.
commodity_wording.MANDARIN: The observed deterioration of the Mandarin fruits is consistent with a transit period that exceeded the recommended shelf life for this commodity. Mandarins from the southern hemisphere have a recommended transit period of approximately 21–35 days depending on variety and harvest date.
commodity_wording.ORANGE: The observed deterioration of the Orange fruits is consistent with an extended transit duration. Oranges have a recommended commercial shelf life of 4–6 weeks; delays in container discharge, customs clearance, or CFS transfer would cumulatively reduce the residual shelf life available upon delivery.
commodity_wording.PEAR: The observed breakdown of the Pear fruits is consistent with an extended transit duration in excess of the recommended commercial shelf life for this variety. The delay would have allowed natural ethylene production to progress ripening past the commercial optimum.
commodity_wording.BLUEBERRY: The observed condition of the Blueberry fruits is consistent with an extended transit and storage period that exceeded the recommended shelf life for this commodity. Fresh blueberries have a very limited shelf life of approximately 14–21 days under optimal cold chain conditions; any delay results in rapid commercial value loss.
commodity_wording.CHERRY: The observed deterioration of the Cherry fruits is consistent with an extended transit duration. Cherries are among the most perishable of tree fruits with a shelf life of approximately 14–21 days under optimal cold chain management; transit delays compound post-harvest decay dramatically.
commodity_wording.PLUM: The observed condition of the Plum fruits is consistent with a transit duration that extended beyond the optimal commercial shelf life window for this commodity. Plums have a recommended cold chain shelf life of 4–6 weeks; any cumulative delay in transit, port discharge, or delivery reduces residual shelf life.
commodity_wording.DRAGON: The observed deterioration of the Dragon Fruits is consistent with an extended transit period. Dragon fruit has a shelf life of approximately 15–25 days under optimal cold storage conditions; transit delays result in scale browning, skin breakdown, and accelerated decay.
commodity_wording.AVOCADO: The observed deterioration of the Avocado fruits is consistent with an extended transit duration. Avocado is a climacteric fruit with a shelf life of 4–6 weeks under optimal conditions; any transit delay that triggers premature ethylene-driven ripening initiation will result in rapid and irreversible softening.
commodity_wording._DEFAULT: The observed deterioration of the subject cargo is consistent with an extended transit period that exceeded the recommended shelf life window for this commodity. Cumulative delays in transit, port discharge, customs clearance, or CFS transfer would have reduced the residual commercial life of the consignment.

IMPROPER_PACKING.label: Improper Packing / Pre-Shipment Packing Deficiency
IMPROPER_PACKING.description: Packaging insufficiency, bruising from handling at origin, or inadequate cushioning

commodity_wording.APPLE: The observed mechanical bruising, pressure marks, and epidermal browning of the Apple fruits is consistent with a pre-shipment packing deficiency. Insufficient cushioning within cartons, overloading of cartons beyond recommended layer counts, or damage sustained during packing line operations at origin would result in the type of localized mechanical injury observed.
commodity_wording.GRAPE: The observed berry splitting, bunch compression damage, and carton base berry accumulation of the Table Grapes is consistent with over-packing or improper carton fill weight at origin. Excessive compression during transit, combined with insufficient SO₂ pad placement, would result in the observed damage pattern.
commodity_wording.KIWI: The observed surface pressure marks, skin bruising, and contact damage of the Kiwi fruits is consistent with a pre-shipment packing deficiency. Insufficient tray depth, inadequate inter-fruit cushioning, or vibration during transport from origin would result in the mechanical injury pattern observed.
commodity_wording.MANDARIN: The observed surface bruising, peel splitting, and compression marks on the Mandarin fruits is consistent with over-packing of cartons at origin or inadequate cushioning material between layers, resulting in compressive injury during transit.
commodity_wording.ORANGE: The observed surface bruising, rind splitting, and compression marks of the Orange fruits is consistent with improper packing at origin. Over-filled cartons, inadequate tissue wrapping, or layer count in excess of recommended maximums would produce the observed compressive injury pattern.
commodity_wording.PEAR: The observed surface bruising, flesh browning beneath the skin, and pressure marks of the Pear fruits is consistent with a pre-shipment packing deficiency. Pears are highly susceptible to mechanical injury; inadequate individual wrapping, over-packed carton layers, or vibration during road transport from the orchard would cause the observed injury pattern.
commodity_wording.BLUEBERRY: The observed berry crushing, skin splitting, and juice accumulation in the Blueberry punnets is consistent with over-packing or compressive damage from carton stacking during palletization. Excessive stacking weight on the lower pallet tiers would result in punnet compression and berry damage.
commodity_wording.CHERRY: The observed compression bruising, skin splitting, and juice staining of the Cherry fruits is consistent with improper packing at origin. Cherries are extremely susceptible to mechanical injury; over-packed bags or inadequate carton compartmentalization would result in the observed compressive damage pattern.
commodity_wording.PLUM: The observed pressure bruising, skin splitting, and juice release of the Plum fruits is consistent with a pre-shipment packing deficiency. Over-packing of trays or cartons, or stacking damage during palletization at origin, would result in the compressive injury pattern observed.
commodity_wording.DRAGON: The observed scale damage, skin puncture marks, and bract compression damage of the Dragon Fruits is consistent with inadequate individual fruit wrapping or insufficient inter-fruit cushioning in the carton at origin, resulting in mechanical injury during transit vibration.
commodity_wording.AVOCADO: The observed surface bruising, skin scuffing, and compression marks of the Avocado fruits is consistent with improper packing at origin. Avocados require adequate individual wrapping and appropriate carton fill to prevent compressive injury; deficiencies in packing would result in the observed surface and sub-epidermal bruising.
commodity_wording._DEFAULT: The observed mechanical damage to the subject cargo is consistent with a pre-shipment packing deficiency. Inadequate cushioning, over-packing, or handling damage during packing operations at origin would result in the mechanical injury pattern observed in the consignment.

PRE_HARVEST_DISEASE.label: Pre-Harvest Disease / Fungal Infection
PRE_HARVEST_DISEASE.description: Fungal, bacterial or other disease condition that was latent at origin and manifested during transit

commodity_wording.APPLE: The observed internal mould, core rot, and fungal lesions of the Apple fruits is consistent with a pre-harvest latent infection that was present in the fruit at origin but not externally visible at the time of packing and shipment. Fungal pathogens such as Botrytis cinerea, Penicillium expansum, and Alternaria spp. are common in apple orchards and can progress rapidly under storage and transit conditions.
commodity_wording.GRAPE: The observed grey mould (Botrytis cinerea) development, bunch rot, and berry skin rupture of the Table Grapes is consistent with a latent pre-harvest infection that established prior to harvest and progressed during sea transit. Botrytis is the primary post-harvest pathogen of table grapes and typically colonizes the berry skin during field conditions.
commodity_wording.KIWI: The observed grey mould, stem-end rot, and internal decay of the Kiwi fruits is consistent with a pre-harvest or post-harvest fungal infection. Botrytis cinerea and Sclerotinia spp. are common post-harvest pathogens of kiwi that establish pre-harvest and progress during cold storage and transit.
commodity_wording.MANDARIN: The observed green/blue mould (Penicillium spp.), stem-end rot, and peel decay of the Mandarin fruits is consistent with a pre-harvest or post-harvest fungal infection. Penicillium digitatum and Penicillium italicum are the primary decay pathogens of citrus and typically enter through stem punctures, skin wounds, or natural pores.
commodity_wording.ORANGE: The observed green and blue mould development, rotten spot formation, and stem-end rot of the Orange fruits is consistent with a pre-harvest or post-harvest infection by Penicillium spp. and other citrus pathogens. The mould pattern observed is typical of wounds inflicted during harvesting and grading operations at origin.
commodity_wording.PEAR: The observed internal breakdown, core rot, and fungal colonization of the Pear fruits is consistent with a pre-harvest latent infection by Botrytis cinerea, Penicillium spp., or other common post-harvest pathogens of pear. These infections typically enter during bloom or through surface wounds and become visible after harvest.
commodity_wording.BLUEBERRY: The observed Botrytis (grey mould) development, skin softening, and water-soaked lesions of the Blueberry fruits is consistent with a pre-harvest latent infection that established in the field prior to harvest. Blueberry is highly susceptible to Botrytis cinerea, and cool, humid field conditions promote spore colonization of the calyx and skin.
commodity_wording.CHERRY: The observed brown rot, surface mould, and skin splitting of the Cherry fruits is consistent with a pre-harvest infection by Monilinia fructicola or other cherry post-harvest pathogens. Cherry is highly susceptible to brown rot, which establishes during the final stages of fruit development in the field.
commodity_wording.PLUM: The observed brown rot (Monilinia fructicola), mummification, and surface mould of the Plum fruits is consistent with a pre-harvest latent infection present at the time of harvest and packing. Stone fruits are highly susceptible to Monilinia brown rot, which can progress rapidly under storage conditions.
commodity_wording.DRAGON: The observed surface mould, scale tip rot, and flesh discoloration of the Dragon Fruits is consistent with a fungal infection (Alternaria spp., Colletotrichum spp.) that was present at a latent stage at origin. Dragon fruit is susceptible to several post-harvest diseases that can establish pre-harvest and progress during storage and transit.
commodity_wording.AVOCADO: The observed anthracnose (Colletotrichum gloeosporioides), stem-end rot, and pulp discoloration of the Avocado fruits is consistent with a pre-harvest latent infection. Avocado anthracnose and stem-end rot are common post-harvest diseases that colonize the fruit pre-harvest and become symptomatic during ripening in storage and transit.
commodity_wording._DEFAULT: The observed fungal decay and disease symptoms of the subject cargo is consistent with a pre-harvest or post-harvest latent infection that was present in the consignment at the time of shipment and progressed during storage and transit. The disease pattern observed is consistent with common post-harvest fungal pathogens of this commodity.

MECHANICAL_INJURY.label: Mechanical Injury / Handling Damage
MECHANICAL_INJURY.description: Physical bruising, impact damage, or abrasion from handling operations (loading, transit, unloading)

commodity_wording.APPLE: The observed surface bruising, epidermal browning, and sub-epidermal discoloration of the Apple fruits is consistent with mechanical injury sustained during handling operations. Apple fruits are susceptible to impact bruising; rough handling during palletizing, container loading, discharge operations, or forklift manoeuvres in the CFS yard would result in the type of localized bruising observed.
commodity_wording.GRAPE: The observed berry splitting, skin abrasion, and stem detachment of the Table Grapes is consistent with mechanical handling damage sustained during loading, transit vibration, or discharge operations. The vibration forces during long-haul transit are a known cause of berry shatter and skin splitting in table grape consignments.
commodity_wording.KIWI: The observed surface scuffing, epidermal peeling, and impact bruising of the Kiwi fruits is consistent with mechanical handling damage. Kiwi skin is fragile when the fruit is ripe; handling forces during carton stacking, palletization, or rough sorting operations at the CFS would result in the observed surface damage.
commodity_wording.MANDARIN: The observed peel splitting, surface abrasion, and compression marks of the Mandarin fruits is consistent with mechanical injury during handling. Rough handling during container destuffing, pallet sorting, or forklift operations at the CFS yard would result in compressive and abrasive injuries to the thin peel of Mandarin fruits.
commodity_wording.ORANGE: The observed rind bruising, oil cell rupture, and surface abrasion of the Orange fruits is consistent with mechanical handling damage sustained during handling operations. Oil cell rupture from impact results in the characteristic browning of the peel observed in mechanically damaged citrus.
commodity_wording.PEAR: The observed impact bruising, flesh discoloration, and surface indentations of the Pear fruits is consistent with mechanical injury. Pears are exceptionally sensitive to impact bruising; even minor handling forces during container discharge, tipping, or CFS movement would result in significant sub-epidermal bruising.
commodity_wording.BLUEBERRY: The observed berry crushing, juice staining, and skin rupture of the Blueberry fruits is consistent with compressive mechanical damage sustained during handling. Blueberry punnets and cartons are susceptible to stack compression damage in the lower tiers of pallets during transit and CFS storage.
commodity_wording.CHERRY: The observed impact bruising, pitting, and skin splitting of the Cherry fruits is consistent with mechanical handling damage. Cherry fruits are among the most susceptible stone fruits to mechanical injury; even low-energy impacts cause sub-epidermal bruising that manifests as darkening and tissue breakdown.
commodity_wording.PLUM: The observed surface bruising, skin splitting, and juice weeping of the Plum fruits is consistent with mechanical handling damage. Plum skin is thin and readily damaged by compressive or impact forces during handling operations, resulting in immediate surface bruising and subsequent rapid tissue breakdown.
commodity_wording.DRAGON: The observed scale damage, skin puncture marks, and surface abrasion of the Dragon Fruits is consistent with mechanical handling damage. Dragon fruit scales are fragile and susceptible to abrasion during carton movement and rough handling during unloading and CFS operations.
commodity_wording.AVOCADO: The observed surface scuffing, skin bruising, and compression marks of the Avocado fruits is consistent with mechanical handling damage. Avocado skin, particularly in riper fruit, is susceptible to abrasion and compressive damage during container unloading, carton sorting, and CFS destuffing operations.
commodity_wording._DEFAULT: The observed mechanical bruising and surface damage of the subject cargo is consistent with physical handling impact sustained during loading, transit, or unloading operations. The pattern of bruising and abrasion is consistent with rough handling practices during container stuffing, vessel transit vibration, or CFS discharge operations.

SELL_IMMEDIATELY.label: Sell Immediately to Mitigate Loss
SELL_IMMEDIATELY.text: To mitigate losses from the damaged {COMMODITY} cargo, we advised the Consignees to sell the consignment immediately at the best available market price, to avoid further deterioration and consequential value loss.

COLD_CHAIN_REINSTATE.label: Maintain / Reinstate Cold Chain
COLD_CHAIN_REINSTATE.text: We advised the Consignees to maintain the subject cargo in cold storage at the recommended temperature range and to ensure the cold chain is reinstated immediately to arrest further deterioration of the remaining sound portion.

NOTICE_TO_CARRIER.label: Lodge Notice of Claim with Carrier
NOTICE_TO_CARRIER.text: Consignees are requested to lodge a formal Notice of Claim against the Ocean Carrier / Shipping Line within the statutory time limit, holding them liable for all transit losses and expenses. A copy of the Surveyor's Report should accompany the Notice of Claim.

FURTHER_SURVEY.label: Reserve Right for Supplementary / Final Report
FURTHER_SURVEY.text: We reserve the right to modify, add to, or supplement this report once additional supporting documentation (including temperature recorder printouts, sale proceeds statements, customs assessment orders, and purchase invoices) is received and reviewed.

SALVAGE_DISPOSAL.label: Arrange Salvage Disposal
SALVAGE_DISPOSAL.text: To minimize further loss to the remaining damaged cargo, we advised the Consignees to arrange salvage disposal at the best available market price through a reputable local dealer, and to maintain proper records of the salvage proceeds for claim quantification purposes.

CLAIM_FROM_CARRIER.label: Pursue Claim Against Responsible Parties
CLAIM_FROM_CARRIER.text: Consignees are requested to pursue the claim directly against the responsible parties (Shipping Line, Freight Forwarder, or other bailees as applicable) with the full supporting documents, and to keep Insurers advised of all developments.

OBTAIN_TEMPERATURE_RECORDS.label: Obtain Temperature Recorder Downloads
OBTAIN_TEMPERATURE_RECORDS.text: We have requested the Consignees / Shipping Line to provide us with the complete temperature recorder download from the reefer container for our analysis. We shall comment further on the temperature findings in our Final Report once the download is received.
